Usage: gaia extract submit [OPTIONS] [PDF]

 Submit a local PDF or parser markdown for knowledge extraction.

 POST /parse/task.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│   pdf      [PDF]  Local PDF to extract (max 64 MiB; 50-page reject is        │
│                   PDF-only).                                                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --content               TEXT     API content field: path, @file, or literal  │
│                                  markdown (file is read locally). Skips LAS  │
│                                  OCR. Prefer also passing the PDF; that      │
│                                  raises the chance of a cache hit.           │
│ --md5                   TEXT     PDF MD5 (32-char hex). Content-only: you    │
│                                  may pass it. Unused when a PDF is given.    │
│ --page                  INTEGER  Optional. Unused when a PDF is given.       │
│ --index,--server        TEXT     Configured LKM index id. [default: bohrium] │
│ --wait                           Poll until the task reaches a terminal      │
│                                  state.                                      │
│ --poll-interval         FLOAT    Seconds between polls when --wait is set;   │
│                                  must be between 1 and 300 (the 5s default   │
│                                  matches the service).                       │
│                                  [default: 5.0]                              │
│ --timeout               FLOAT    Seconds to wait before giving up when       │
│                                  --wait is set; must be greater than 0 and   │
│                                  at most 86400.                              │
│                                  [default: 1800.0]                           │
│ --out                   PATH     Write JSON to PATH (atomic) instead of      │
│                                  stdout.                                     │
│ --no-hint                        Suppress Gaia follow-up suggestions on      │
│                                  stderr.                                     │
│ --help                           Show this message and exit.                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

 Examples:
 gaia extract submit paper.pdf
 gaia extract submit paper.pdf --content paper.md
 gaia extract submit --content paper.md --md5 <32-hex> --page 12
 What you have:
 a local PDF, return the task id now  ->  submit
 a local PDF, block until terminal    ->  submit --wait
 parser markdown                      ->  --content (path, @file, or literal)
 content-only, try the PDF cache      ->  --content --md5, optional --page
 already have a task_id               ->  status / result
 --content is the API text field, not a second file part. A path or @file is
 read locally and posted as content. Even with --content, pass the PDF when you
 have it: that raises the chance of a cache hit and skips LAS OCR. --md5 is the
 PDF's 32-char hex digest; use it on content-only submits. --page is optional.
 When a PDF is given, both flags are unused — do not pass them. The 50-page
 reject applies only to PDF-only submits.
 Use this when the paper may not be in the LKM corpus yet. Resubmitting the
 same PDF or `--content` body reuses the existing extraction rather than
 starting over, so an already-processed paper comes back terminal immediately
 with `cache_hit`. `cache_source` says where that reuse came from: `lkm` when
 the paper was already extracted in the corpus, `local` when an earlier
 submission of this same PDF or `--content` body produced it. Resubmitting will
 not hurry a running task along: the same user sending the same PDF or
 `--content` body while it is still queued or running returns business error
 290020 with the existing task_id.
 Without --wait, submit returns immediately with the full submit envelope on
 stdout (not just the task id). Save `data.task_id` from it and poll with `gaia
 extract status`, or pass --wait to have this command poll for you.
